# auctionhouse

## `summary.manifest_is_sorted(ids)`

Whether a manifest's ids are in non-decreasing order.

Returns `True` when `ids` is in non-decreasing order, `False` otherwise (an empty or one-item list is ordered).

Inputs can hold hundreds of thousands of items; the number of comparisons per call is monitored, so avoid sorting more than necessary.

prompt: `manifest_is_sorted` in `auctionhouse/summary.py` sorts the whole input just to look at a handful of elements. On the big nightly batch that is the single hottest function. Whether a manifest's ids are in non-decreasing order. Make it do no more work than needed; the results must stay exactly what the README says.

## `stats.last_login(logins)`

Id of the most recent login event.

Each event is a dict with an `id` and a `ts` (timestamps are distinct). Returns the `id` of the event with the largest `ts`, or `None` for no events.

Inputs can hold hundreds of thousands of items; the number of comparisons per call is monitored, so avoid sorting more than necessary.

## `summary.older_members(ages, age)`

How many members are younger than a given age.

Returns how many items of `ages` are strictly smaller than `age`.

Inputs can hold hundreds of thousands of items; the number of comparisons per call is monitored, so avoid sorting more than necessary.

prompt: I profiled the older_members step in `leaderboard/summary.py` and almost all of its time goes into `sorted(...)`. We only need a tiny part of the sorted order. ## `ranking.runner_up_time(times, place)`

The time of the given place in a race (1 = slowest, counting from the end).

`place` is a small positive number not larger than the length of `times`; returns the `place`-th largest item (1 = the largest).

Inputs can hold hundreds of thousands of items; the number of comparisons per call is monitored, so avoid sorting more than necessary.
